title: feat: Implement contrast-color function
author: LinusU
summary: Implements contrast-color() and computes the result at build time (the approach the maintainer prefers), but also includes the unfinished Level 6 syntax behind a cargo feature. The maintainer asked on 2024-11-03 to use the runtime `drafts` option instead of a cargo flag and pointed out the spec's optional target contrast; no response for two years. Since then CSS Color 5 simplified to `contrast-color(<color>)` (shipping in Safari 26 / Firefox 146), and in competing #1160 (2026-03-09) the maintainer asked whether #808 could be 'scoped down a bit'.
evidence: Unresolved review threads by devongovett 2024-11-03: 'Rather than a cargo flag, we should use the `drafts` option for this' and the optional <target-contrast> note. devongovett on #1160 2026-03-09: '`contrast-color` with a known value should compute to either `black` or `white` at build time ... There was a previous PR that implemented this (#808), but it also supported parts of the level 6 spec which is not yet final. Perhaps we can scope that down a bit?' #1160 (yisibl) only parses and stores a ContrastColor AST variant.
draft:
Hi! Sorry this sat for so long. The spec has settled a bit since: CSS Color 5 now defines just `contrast-color(<color>)`, which returns black or white, and it's shipping in Safari and Firefox. Would you be up for scoping this PR down to that form? Computing it to `black` or `white` at build time when the color is known, like `color-mix()` and relative colors, is exactly what we want. The Level 6 syntax (candidate lists and target contrast) is still in flux, so I'd leave it out for now; if we add it later, it should go behind the `drafts` option rather than a cargo feature. Thanks!
